# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1114

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃1114화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|찰나지간 공간을 가로지른 빛줄기는 눈부셨고, 동시에 파괴적이었다.
  6|
  7|적수공권의 상태에서도 수비군들을 무참히 도륙하던 혈주가, 허리춤에 얌전히 잠들어 있던 자신의 애도(愛刀)를 움직였을 만큼.
  8|
  9|콰아아앙!
 10|
 11|커다란 굉음과 함께 사방으로 흩뿌려지는 핏물.
 12|
 13|그러나 지금까지와는 달리, 그 피의 근원지는 수비군이 아닌 혈주를 따르던 광신도들이었다.
 14|
 15|“쿠, 쿨럭. 혈주시여…….”
 16|
 17|과연 운이 좋았다고 해야 할까, 아니면 나쁘다고 해야 할까.
 18|
 19|기습적으로 날아든 섬광의 여파에 휩쓸려 비명조차 지르지 못하고 절명한 수십여 명의 동료와는 달리, 가까스로 목숨을 보전한 광신도는 혈주를 향해 기어갔다.
 20|
 21|천주의 선택을 받은 위대한 사도(使徒)가, 이 고통을 조금이라도 덜어 주길 바라면서.
 22|
 23|그리고 혈주는 그 간절한 부름에 응답했다.
 24|
 25|천근(千斤)의 무게가 실린 발끝으로.
 26|
 27|콰득!
 28|
 29|척추가 으스러지는 소리가 났고, 그것으로 끝이었다.
 30|
 31|그가 꺼져 가는 생명의 지푸라기라도 잡고 싶었는지, 아니면 죽음을 통한 안식을 원했는지는 혈주도 몰랐다.
 32|
 33|아니, 소모품이나 다름없는 조무래기의 죽음 따위는 애초부터 관심 밖의 일이었다는 것이 옳은 표현이었다.
 34|
 35|혈주의 시선은 처음부터 줄곧, 자욱하게 피어오른 먼지구름 너머에 고정되어 있었으니까.
 36|
 37|“나와.”
 38|
 39|서늘한 목소리가 혈주의 입술 밖으로 흘러나온 그 순간.
 40|
 41|슈확!
 42|
 43|불현듯 뻗어 나온 섬광이 먼지구름을 쪼개며 혈주를 향해 쇄도했다.
 44|
 45|정확히는, 섬광처럼 빛나는 열기가.
 46|
 47|화륵, 콰아아아아!
 48|
 49|이글거리며 공간을 휩쓸어오는 불길.
 50|
 51|의심을 확신으로 만드는 그 끔찍할 열기는 느끼며, 혈주는 전력을 다해 적도(赤刀)를 내리그었다.
 52|
 53|서걱!
 54|
 55|예리한 절삭음과 함께 좌우로 갈라지는 화염.
 56|
 57|그 폭만 이십여 장에 달하는 대로변이 삽시간에 불길에 휩싸이고, 거세게 피어오르는 아지랑이 사이로 한 사람의 그림자가 일렁였다.
 58|
 59|“어딜 그리 급하게 가느냐.”
 60|
 61|착 가라앉은 음성.
 62|
 63|그리고 아지랑이 속에서도 또렷하게 빛나는, 화염을 쏟아내고 있는 두 눈동자.
 64|
 65|화왕(火王) 적천강.
 66|
 67|바로 그였다.
 68|
 69|아직은 나타나지 못할 것이라 여겼던, 혹은 어쩌면 영영 두 번 다시 보지 못하리라 생각했던 그의 모습에 혈주의 눈매가 가늘어졌다.
 70|
 71|“정파 놈들이 그토록 칭송하던 십왕(十王)의 수좌도 결국 한낱 무부였군. 하나뿐인 제자를 살리고 싶어 그 많은 아군을 버렸나?”
 72|
 73|북문을 버리고 왔다고 확신한 혈주의 비아냥에, 적천강이 거친 숨을 가다듬으며 입을 열었다.
 74|
 75|“칭송해 달라고 부탁한 적도 없지만, 모든 것에는 그만한 이유가 있는 법이지.”
 76|
 77|“뭐?”
 78|
 79|“일천의 마병(魔兵)을 쓰러트린 그 날부터 천하는 노부를 화왕이라 부르기 시작했지. 하도 오래되었다 보니 별호가 슬슬 지겨워지던 참인데…… 어쩌면 오늘 이후로 바뀔 수도 있겠다는 생각이 드는군.”
 80|
 81|“……!”
 82|
 83|일순간, 비로소 적천강의 등장이 무엇을 의미하는지 깨달은 혈주의 얼굴이 일그러졌다.
 84|
 85|북문으로 향한 포달랍궁의 전력은 분명 강력했다.
 86|
 87|서장 제일의 고수인 달뢰라마와, 비록 애송이에 불과하지만 초절정 고수가 둘이나 포함되어 있던 십이밀승.
 88|
 89|거기에 혹시 모를 상황을 대비하여 두 기의 흑귀를 보냈으니, 적천강의 발을 묶는 것을 넘어 그의 숨통을 끊어도 이상하지 않을 정도였다.
 90|
 91|‘그런데, 도대체 어떻게?’
 92|
 93|자신도 모르게 뇌리를 스친 그 의문에 대한 답을, 혈주는 쉽게 찾을 수 없었다.
 94|
 95|아니, 어쩌면 앞으로도 영영 알 수 없을 것이다.
 96|
 97|무언가를 지키기 위해 싸우는 자와, 오로지 복수에 눈이 먼 자의 싸움은 종종 예상을 한참 빗나가기도 한다는 것을.
 98|
 99|그리고 화왕 적천강에게는, 자신의 모든 것을 바쳐서라도 지켜야 할 사람이 있었다.
100|
101|“고작, 그따위 땡중들로 노부의 발걸음을 막을 수 있으리라 생각했더냐.”
102|
103|귓가를 파고드는 나직한 음성에, 혈주는 이를 악물었다.
104|
105|“미친 늙은이 같으니. 네놈이 아무리 발악해 봤자 달라지는 건 아무것도 없다.”
106|
107|“지켰고, 지킬 것이다.”
108|
109|“지금 이 순간에도 죽어 가고 있을, 그 소중한 제자를 말이냐?”
110|
111|“……뭐라?”
112|
113|본능적으로 멈칫한 적천강을 향해, 혈주는 입매를 비틀며 웃었다.
114|
115|“아니. 아니지. 어쩌면 이미 죽었을 수도 있겠군. 마지막으로 보았을 때 이미 사경을 헤매고 있었으니.”
116|
117|“네놈이 감히……!”
118|
119|그리고 제자의 위기를 전해 들은 적천강이 도무지 감출 수 없는 격동에 휩싸인 그 순간.
120|
121|쉭!
122|
123|희미한 파공성과 함께, 허깨비처럼 사라진 혈주의 신형이 십여 장의 거리를 지우며 들이닥쳤다.
124|
125|서걱!
126|
127|마치 두부처럼 갈라지는 지면.
128|
129|그와 동시에, 가까스로 신형을 비틀어 공격을 피해 낸 적천강의 몸 곳곳에서 핏물이 솟구쳤다.
130|
131|투두둑!
132|
133|스치는 것만으로도 피해를 불러일으키는 막강한 검압(劍壓).
134|
135|그러나 허공으로 비산하는 저 핏물에 담긴 의미가 무엇인지, 적천강 본인은 누구보다 잘 알고 있었다.
136|
137|‘몸이……!’
138|
139|천근처럼 무겁다. 감각을 통한 반응 역시 늦었다.
140|
141|적천강은 분노와 다급함으로 인해 잠시 잊고 있었던 중요한 사실을 깨달았다.
142|
143|북문에서의 힘겨운 전투를 끝마친 자신의 육신이 얼마나 지쳐있었는지.
144|
145|찰나지간 주체할 수 없을 만큼 흔들려 버린 마음이, 지금 같은 생사결에서 얼마나 심각한 악영향을 초래하는지.
146|
147|그리고 이와 같은 적천강을 상황을, 혈주는 정확히 꿰뚫어 보았다.
148|
149|콰아아아아!
150|
151|폭풍처럼 휘몰아치는 도격(刀擊)이 공간을 난도질한다.
152|
153|수십, 아니 수백 합에 달하는 공격이 시간마저 쪼개며 서로를 향해 퍼부어졌고, 이미 지칠 대로 지친 적천강은 이 싸움의 끝이 얼마 남지 않았다는 사실을 본능적으로 직감할 수 있었다.
154|
155|그 끝에 기다리고 있을 싸움의 결과가 자신의 죽음이며, 이를 뒤바꿀 수 있는 유일한 패가 남아 있다는 것 역시도.
156|
157|‘화신귀무(火神鬼武).’
158|
159|스스로의 모든 것을 장작 삼아 피워 올리는 최후의 불꽃.
160|
161|열화문 대대로 전해져 내려오는, 그러나 동시에 그 끔찍한 여파로 인해 금기(禁忌)시되어 온 신공.
162|
163|이미 그로 인해 죽을 고비를 넘긴 적천강이었으나, 이제 그에게 남은 것은 그것뿐이었다.
164|
165|회복을 넘어 재생에 가까운 힘을 발휘하는 혈주를 쓰러트릴 방법은.
166|
167|하지만 그 짧은 고민의 시간조차, 매 순간이 위기나 다름없는 지금의 적천강에게는 사치였을지 몰랐다.
168|
169|‘빈틈!’
170|
171|혈주의 안광이 번뜩인 그 찰나의 순간.
172|
173|후우웅!
174|
175|지면에 깊게 박힌 적도 대신, 전력을 다해 휘두른 일권(一拳)이 적천강의 옆구리를 향해 포탄처럼 쏘아졌다.
176|
177|진태경의 일섬에 의해 위기에 빠진 이후, 어째서인지 더욱 강력해진 힘과 속도로.
178|
179|“……!”
180|
181|적천강에게는 헛숨을 삼킬 시간조차 주어지지 않았다.
182|
183|이미 육신은 지쳤고, 감각은 무뎌졌으며, 공력은 어느덧 바닥을 드러내고 있는 상황.
184|
185|그저 온 힘을 다해 강기가 담긴 두 팔을 교차시키는 것만이, 그가 할 수 있는 최선이었다.
186|
187|콰아아앙!
188|
189|거대한 굉음과 함께 뒤집히는 시야.
190|
191|순식간에 십여 장에 달하는 공간을 가로질러 내쏘아진 적천강의 신형이, 한때는 사람들로 붐볐을 커다란 객잔을 뚫고 처박혔다.
192|
193|콰드드득!
194|
195|기둥이 무너지고, 나뭇조각이 비산한다.
196|
197|객잔을 시작으로 무려 일곱 채에 달하는 건물을 박살 낸 뒤에야, 적천강은 뱃속에서 울컥 치밀어오르는 뜨거운 무언가를 토해 냈다.
198|
199|푸화악.
200|
201|어딘지 모를 뒷골목을 적시는, 까맣게 죽은 사혈(死血).
202|
203|그리고 흐릿해지는 시야 속, 질풍처럼 쇄도하는 혈주의 모습이 그의 시야에 들어왔다.
204|
205|그 핏빛 눈동자에 담긴, 희열과 살기도 함께.
206|
207|“적천강-!”
208|
209|포효하듯 부르짖은 혈주가 적도를 내리그은 그 순간이었다.
210|
211|카아아앙!
212|
213|날카롭게 울려 퍼지는 굉음.
214|
215|예상치도 못한 시점에 사각(斜脚)에서 쏘아진, 다섯 줄기의 섬광을 튕겨 내며 뒷걸음질 친 혈주가 믿을 수 없다는 듯이 눈을 부릅떴다.
216|
217|우우웅.
218|
219|손아귀를 통해 전해지는 울림.
220|
221|부르르 떨리는 적도(赤刀)는 금세 안정을 되찾았지만, 이미 악귀처럼 일그러진 혈주의 얼굴은 펴지지 않았다.
222|
223|“제법이긴 한데…… 그만큼 나이를 처먹었으면 나설 때 안 나설 때 정도는 구분해야지. 그렇지 않나?”
224|
225|으르렁거리는 듯한 음성과 함께 서서히 돌아가는 고개.
226|
227|동시에 혈주의 핏빛 안광이, 어느덧 적천강의 앞을 가로막은 다섯 명의 노인을 향해 번뜩였다.
228|
229|“사지가 찢겨 뒈지기 싫으면.”
230|
231|그러나 그 막강한 살기에도, 그들의 중심에 선 호리호리한 체구의 노 도사는 조용히 적천강을 부축했다.
232|
233|화아악.
234|
235|부축과 동시에 스며드는 공력에, 창백하기 그지없던 얼굴 위로 감돌기 시작하는 혈색.
236|
237|다시 한번 울컥 피를 토해 내는 적천강에게, 노도사가 담담한 음성으로 입을 열었다.
238|
239|“고생하셨습니다. 지금부터 이곳은 저희가 맡지요.”
240|
241|“쿨럭, 자네들은…….”
242|
243|“진태경, 그 아이에게 남아 있는 시간이 그리 길지 않을지도 모릅니다.”
244|
245|“……!”
246|
247|“가십시오, 어서. 이것이 모두를 위한 길이기도 합니다.”
248|
249|물론, 노 도사의 입술 사이로 흘러나온 ‘모두’라는 단어에는 한 사람의 존재가 빠져 있었다.
250|
251|“허, 미친 늙은이가 여섯으로 늘어났군.”
252|
253|비웃음과 함께, 혈주는 적도를 비스듬히 내리그었다.
254|
255|“그렇다면, 전부 죽어라.”
256|
257|슈화악!
258|
259|반월의 형태를 한 핏빛 강기가 적도를 타고 쏘아졌다.
260|
261|강기의 크기만 무려 일장에 달하는, 끔찍하리만치 강대한 기운이 담긴 일격.
262|
263|그리고 바로 다음 순간.
264|
265|꽈아아앙!
266|
267|하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음과 함께, 반경 십여 장의 공간 전체가 가루가 되어 흩날렸다.
268|
269|어느샌가 아득한 허공을 밟고 서 있는, 여섯 개의 인영 아래에서.
270|
271|“……!”
272|
273|혈주의 눈빛이 깊게 가라앉은 그때, 예의 그 호리호리한 노 도사가 자신이 부축하고 있던 적천강을 향해 작게 고개를 숙였다.
274|
275|“부디, 이 까마득한 후배의 무례를 용서하시길.”
276|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{

"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*BOOM!*

[P86]
His vision overturned.

[P87]
The blow hurled Jeok more than ten jang through the air and straight through a large inn that had once been crowded with people.

[P88]
*CRASH!*

[P89]
A pillar collapsed. Splinters flew.

[P90]
Not until he had smashed through seven buildings, beginning with the inn, did Jeok cough up the hot surge rising from his gut.

[P91]
*Splatter.*

[P92]
Blackened blood stained an alley he didn’t recognize.

[P93]
Through his blurring vision, he saw the Blood Lord rushing toward him like a gale. Joy and killing intent burned together in those blood-red eyes.

[P94]
“Jeok Cheongang!”

[P95]
The Blood Lord roared his name and brought the Red Blade down.

[P96]
*CLANG!*

[P97]
A sharp crash rang out.

[P98]
Five streaks of light had come from an unexpected angle. The Blood Lord deflected them and stumbled back, his eyes wide with disbelief.

[P99]
*Whoooom.*

[P100]
A vibration ran through his grip.

[P101]
The Red Blade trembled, then steadied. The Blood Lord’s face, twisted like a Fiend’s, did not.

[P102]
“Not bad…… But after living this long, you ought to know when to stay out of a fight. Don’t you think?”

[P103]
He slowly turned his head as he growled.

[P104]
His blood-red gaze fell on the five old men standing between him and Jeok Cheongang.

[P105]
“Unless you want your limbs torn off.”

[P106]
Despite the killing intent bearing down on them, the slender old Daoist at their center quietly helped Jeok to his feet.

[P107]
*Fwoosh.*

[P108]
Internal energy flowed into Jeok, and a little color returned to his deathly pale face. He coughed up another mouthful of blood.

[P109]
“Thank you for all your hard work,” the old Daoist said calmly. “We’ll take it from here.”

[P110]
“Cough. You’re……”

[P111]
“Jin Taekyung may not have much time left.”

[P112]
“……!”

[P113]
“Go. Quickly. It’s for everyone’s sake.”

[P114]
Of course, the old Daoist’s “everyone” left out one person.

[P115]
“Ha. Now there are six crazy old men.”

[P116]
Sneering, the Blood Lord angled the Red Blade downward.

[P117]
“Then you can all die.”

[P118]
*Whoosh!*

[P119]
A crescent of blood-red Force shot from the blade. The Force alone measured a full jang, and the power within it was terrifying.

[P120]
The next instant—

[P121]
*BOOM!*

[P122]
A crash like the sky splitting apart rang out. Everything within a ten-jang radius crumbled to dust.

[P123]
Above it stood six figures, high in the air.

[P124]
“……!”

[P125]
The Blood Lord’s gaze darkened. The slender old Daoist bowed his head slightly to Jeok Cheongang, whom he had been supporting.

[P126]
“Please forgive the impertinence of one so far your junior.”

[P127]
Jeok was too drained to answer. Severe exhaustion and Internal Injury had been building since the North Gate.

[P128]
No—there wasn’t even time for an answer. Before he could speak, the old Daoist’s arms swung with force.

[P129]
“You crazy—!”

[P130]
The Blood Lord’s frantic shout came too late.

[P131]
*Whoooosh!*

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang shot through the air toward the Inner City.

[P133]
Before the enraged Blood Lord could pursue him, the five old Daoists landed softly on the ground and blocked his way.

[P134]
They had the bearing of immortals, an aura like noble cranes, and a movement technique astonishing enough to match.

[P135]
Only then did the Blood Lord recognize the intruders.

[P136]
“The Kunlun Five Immortals.”

[P137]
“You know us?”

[P138]
“How could I not? I’ve heard the heartbreaking tale of five old men who should have died long ago, still eating up the Kunlun Sect’s rice.”

[P139]
Naturally, the Blood Lord’s account bore little resemblance to their reputation.

[P140]
The Kunlun Five Immortals were Martial Uncles to Cheongheoja, the current Sect Leader, and Elders who still upheld the Kunlun Sect well into their eighties.

[P141]
Each had stopped just short of Supreme Peak. But they had grown up as close as brothers, and their combined technique was said to withstand even a Supreme Peak master.

[P142]
To the Blood Lord, they were merely five more troublesome old moths.

[P143]
“Get out of my sight. I’d tear you apart right now, but even that would waste time.”

[P144]
The slender old Daoist, the eldest of the Kunlun Five Immortals, shook his head.

[P145]
“I cannot accept that offer. So I’d like to suggest an alternative.”

[P146]
“There is no alternative. You’ve just thrown away your last chance.”

[P147]
The Blood Lord let the Red Blade hang at an angle and stepped toward them.

[P148]
First Jin Taekyung. Now Jeok Cheongang. Twice he had lost prey he’d nearly caught—prey he had to kill.

[P149]
Their auras felt far stronger than their reputations suggested. That was puzzling, but even a combined technique capable of facing a Supreme Peak master would be a tower built on sand before him. It would fall in moments.

[P150]
He was certain of it.

[P151]
“You’re mistaken,” the old Daoist said. “We still have a chance.”

[P152]
“What?”

[P153]
“This is the alternative we came up with.”

[P154]
Only then did the Blood Lord notice the calm smile on Perfected One Taecheong’s lips. Something was wrong.

[P155]
*Shaaaaa.*

[P156]
Power surged from Perfected One Taecheong—no, from all five of the Kunlun Five Immortals—and shook the air around them.

[P157]
No one would have believed these men had stopped at the edge of Peak. Their aura was so fierce it made the *Immortals* in their name seem absurd.

[P158]
It took the Blood Lord little time to recognize what felt so familiar about it.

[P159]
“You…… Don’t tell me.”

[P160]
“It’s as fearsome as I heard, this Temporary Strength Pill.”

[P161]
“……!”

[P162]
“No need to look so surprised. None of us has ever practiced demonic martial arts. We had to pay a price to take it.”

[P163]
Perfected One Taecheong was telling the truth.

[P164]
The Temporary Strength Pill’s power was chiefly for practitioners of demonic, heterodox arts—particularly those whose martial arts remained incomplete because they had not reached Supreme Peak.

[P165]
Even if someone who cultivated pure qi took one of the spare pills carried by Dark Heaven’s followers, it would have little effect.

[P166]
Unless they did something mad: broke the innate qi they had built up over more than eighty years and forced themselves to absorb the pill’s energy.

[P167]
“To stop a monster……”

[P168]
*Whoooom.*

[P169]
His words faded beneath a deep rumble.

[P170]
An unstable, hazy Force gathered around the sword in Perfected One Taecheong’s hand. There was no mistaking what it was.

[P171]
And it wasn’t his sword alone. Force rose from the blades of all five Kunlun Five Immortals.

[P172]
“We’ll gladly become monsters ourselves.”

[P173]
*Whoosh!*

[P174]
Space split, and six figures clashed.

[P175]
* * *

[P176]
Fifteen minutes.

[P177]
That was all the time the Kunlun Five Immortals remained on their feet.

[P178]
But for someone else, they had bought a full fifteen minutes.

[P179]
Perhaps that was why Perfected One Taecheong could smile even through the overwhelming pain as both his legs were torn off.

[P180]
*Slice!*

[P181]
Then his arms were severed.

[P182]
*Boom!*

[P183]
Even as the organs inside him tore apart, he swallowed his screams.

[P184]
And when the shadow of death finally fell over him, the old Daoist held fast to his principles and offered a last farewell to his Junior Brothers, whose breathing had already ceased.

[P185]
“Remember…… Our deaths will not be in vain……”

[P186]
*Crack!*

[P187]
Brain matter sprayed with a horrible sound.

[P188]
The Blood Lord lifted his foot from Perfected One Taecheong’s shattered head.

[P189]
“No,” he whispered coldly. “You died for nothing.”

[P190]
As he slowly raised his head, cries sounded from every direction, louder and closer than before.

[P191]
No. They were a creed of exactly eight characters.

[P192]
*Heaven above and earth below; All demons bow!*

[P193]
Above the heavens, beneath the heavens—let all things kneel.

[P194]
“……And so they shall.”

[P195]
The monster walked on toward the Inner City, sticky blood trailing with him.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
